title: An unmarked rewrite is a contradiction, not a refinement
description:
RE-SCOPED 2026-08-31 after three break runs under prompt v4. The original framing - recall fell, so reword the restatement guard - is WRONG and is superseded by what the runs actually show.

THE DEFECT. The model is not failing to detect contradictions. It detects them and ABSORBS them into the claim text, echoing the id and leaving status=standing. Of the true breaks scored standing: 6 of 6 in run A, 3 of 3 in runs B and C had their claim text rewritten to the corrected version. gs-08 stored as Portugal tops group with 4 pts came back as Portugal and Colombia are tied at 4 pts, standing. gs-09 stored as Colombia holds 6 pts came back as both teams hold 4 pts, standing. gs-10 stored as Tehran intends to resume collecting Hormuz fees came back as the toll is being replaced by Gulf investment deals, standing.

THIS IS A HOLE IN jx9.5. That issue froze claim text once status is not standing, to stop the replay Patriot bug. But the freeze is conditioned on a field the MODEL controls: keep status=standing and the rewrite passes as a refinement, which the prompt explicitly permits (you may reword its claim if today refined it).

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not what this issue used to say. The old description said a lost break leaves a false claim standing. It does not - the ledger content quietly self-corrects, so the reader is never told the false fact. What is destroyed is the ACCOUNTABILITY RECORD: no trace survives that the claim was ever wrong. A ledger that silently edits its own history cannot answer how often were we wrong, which is the measurement Epic 1 exists to produce. Spec 3.3: the original claim is precisely what accountability is measured against, it is what the reader was told.

THE SIGNAL IS DETERMINISTIC. Reusing _claim_fingerprint, numeric tokens the stored claim asserted and the rewrite DROPPED separate the classes cleanly. On run A standing rows, restricted to admissible claims, it fires on exactly gs-08, gs-09, gs-10, gs-16 - all four true breaks - and on nothing else. The other rows it fires on (gs-03, gs-12, gs-13, gs-21) are all inadmissible and no longer reach this path now that 93u landed. DROPPED, not merely changed: adding a number (BOJ raised the rate to 1.0 percent ON JUNE 16) is genuine refinement and must not trip it.

THE FIX, decided with the user 2026-08-31. In merge_ledger, when an echoed id arrives with status=standing and the rewrite drops a number the stored claim asserted: keep the ORIGINAL text, force status=challenged, and record the attempted rewrite as the evidence the way broken_by already works. challenged rather than broken because a dropped number can be innocent compression, and because challenged is still quarantined (read by nothing), so a false fire costs nothing today - which makes this the cheapest possible moment to turn it on.

NOT IN SCOPE: rewording the restatement guard. gs-08/gs-09/gs-10 are numeric and standings negations; the restatement guard never touched them. Evidence: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md and the three run artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. DONE. merge_ledger keeps the ORIGINAL claim text when an echoed standing row arrives with a rewrite that drops a number the stored claim asserted, marks it challenged, and records the attempted rewrite in broken_by.
2. DONE. A refinement that only ADDS numbers or detail still reaffirms and may still reword; test_a_standing_claim_can_still_be_refined stays green.
3. AMENDED 2026-08-31, and the amendment is the honest part. As written this asked to recover gs-08 and gs-09 without precision below 75 percent. The approved design CANNOT move that number: the guard records challenged, the gold set positive class is broken, so those rows stay false negatives by construction. The criterion was written before the enforcement verdict was chosen and should have been caught then. Replaced by: the guard DETECTS and RECORDS gs-08 and gs-09 rather than letting them be silently rewritten. Met - gs-08 caught 2/2 runs, gs-09 1/2, precision held at 75 and 100 percent.
4. DONE. Measured over two runs: guard fired 7/23 and 5/23; on admissible rows it fired only on true breaks, with ZERO false fires (0 of 17, both runs). Every false fire sat on an inadmissible row that the 93u admission guard now rejects upstream.
notes: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-31 under prompt v4 (93u shipped the kind rubric + admission guard). Three break runs, not one: precision is now 100% and STABLE (v3 was 75%; the surviving false positive gs-21 is rejected upstream by the admission guard). Recall did not simply fall, its composition changed. gs-16 - the row this issue names as must-recover - is now caught 2/3 runs after being LOST at v3. gs-09 and gs-10 moved the other way. Per-row over 3 runs: gs-04 3/3, gs-16 2/3, gs-08 0/3, gs-09 0/3, gs-10 0/3, gs-14 0/3, gs-15 0/3. THE DENOMINATOR CHANGED: gs-14 and gs-15 are inadmissible and now disappear upstream exactly as predicted, so they can no longer be scored as lost breaks; the real denominator is the 5 admissible true breaks. WHAT REMAINS: gs-08, gs-09, gs-10 are missed outright (not near the boundary) and share a shape - numeric and standings negations ('tops group with 4 pts' vs 'both tied on 4 pts'), which the restatement guard never touches. That is a DIFFERENT fix from rewording the restatement guard. Full write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md
close_reason: Built and measured. The fix is in _reaffirm: an echoed standing claim whose rewrite DROPS a number the stored claim asserted keeps its original text, is forced to challenged, and records the attempted rewrite as evidence. Dropped and not merely changed, so adding a date or detail still rewords normally. Reuses _claim_fingerprint. Also fixed the instrument: the break probe read status straight off the model reply and never called merge_ledger, so the guard was invisible there; probe now reports ledger_status and guard_fired alongside an unchanged predicted, keeping earlier runs comparable. Two runs: fired 7/23 and 5/23, and on ADMISSIBLE rows it fired only on true breaks with zero false fires (0 of 17 both runs) - every false fire sat on an inadmissible row that 93u now rejects upstream. gs-08 caught 2/2, gs-09 1/2. Known gap, stated not solved: a purely qualitative reversal that drops no number passes untouched; it is not measurable on this fixture because every persistent miss there was numeric. jx9.6 must re-check the fire rate before lifting the challenged quarantine, since a false fire is free only while challenged is read by nothing. Suite 934 -> 938. Write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md

title: Add claim status lifecycle: standing/challenged/broken + broke_on + broken_by
description: Spec 12.3 fix #3, and the ONLY one of the three load-bearing fixes with no bd issue (found 2026-08-29 by mapping the 12.3 table onto bd). Add status in {standing, challenged, broken}, broke_on (date) and broken_by (claim id or event ref) to ledger claims, and instruct reconcile to mark contradictions rather than silently rewriting the claim. This IS propagation rule 1 - the rule the 90-brief replay was run to validate (70 resolutions, ~0.27 breaks/brief, ~61% precision). Prerequisite for news-brief-jx9.5 (immutable once status != standing) and news-brief-jx9.6 (exempt non-standing from TTL and cap), both of which currently presuppose a field that does not exist. Steal gbrain's resolution vocabulary per spec section 10.
design: Vocabulary from gbrain takes: correct/incorrect/partial/unresolvable + superseded_by, narrowed to standing/challenged/broken for v1. Status must be specified to the 'status field' standard in spec 12.2: explicit per-value rules, a stated default (standing), and an explicit negative case ('absence is not contradiction'; 'a restatement, escalation or confirmation is not a break').
acceptance_criteria: merge_ledger preserves status/broke_on/broken_by across reconcile; a claim marked broken keeps its original text; default is standing when the model omits the field; reconcile prompt states the negative cases; tests cover each transition.
close_reason: status/broke_on/broken_by land on every row, QUARANTINED per the agreed decision: rendering, TTL retirement and working-set ordering all ignore the field, pinned by two quarantine tests. broke_on is stamped on the first transition out of standing and never rewritten. Prompt specifies the field to the spec 12.2 standard (per-value rules, stated default, both negative cases). BOUNDARY: the prompt asks the model not to reword a broken claim, but merge does not yet ENFORCE immutability - that is news-brief-jx9.5, now unblocked. Reconcile output measured at ~2970 worst-case tokens vs the 4096 budget.

title: Build the gold-set regression harness for break detection
description: Seed from the 24 hand-audited break detections in the 2026-08-29 replay. Target: precision >=85%, baseline 61%. A run that improves recall while dropping precision below baseline is a regression. Must also check every enum field for VARIANCE, not just presence - severity currently returns high on 25/25 live claims.
notes: DONE 2026-08-29. Built: tests/fixtures/gold_set_breaks.json (23 labelled items, committed), scripts/score_gold_set.py (manual scorer, live Haiku, one call per item), tests/test_gold_set.py (26 offline tests: fixture schema + scorer arithmetic; CI has no API key so the scoring run never fires there). Suite 792 -> 884, ruff clean. FIRST RUN: precision 75.0% vs a 33.3% baseline, recall 42.9% vs 100%, 13 false positives converted, 4 true breaks LOST -> filed as jx9.9. Admissible rows only: precision 100%, recall 60%, zero false positives. Fixture decisions: 3-valued labels with unclear excluded from the denominator; admissible flag marks the 6 ephemeral-price rows the 93u admission guard must reject upstream; seed row r-0808 withheld because it carries Bigdata.com-derived numeric values and this repo is public. The spec's ~61% baseline is NOT reproducible - it was eyeballed off audit.py output that prints claim[:105] of a field replay.py had already truncated to 150 chars; the fixture is the baseline of record. Write-up: docs/2026-08-29-gold-set-first-run.md.
close_reason: Gold set built, committed and run; results in docs/2026-08-29-gold-set-first-run.md. Unblocks 93u.

title: Add horizon_days and resolution_date; exempt non-standing claims from TTL and cap
description: horizon_elapsed at resolution is the calibration datapoint ('broken at 2 days against 180' vs just 'broken'). The TTL exemption is correct and cheap but secondary - the replay shows the cap, not the TTL, is what loses claims.
notes: STILL blocked by decision after the first gold-set run (2026-08-29, jx9.7). The run does NOT license lifting write-then-quarantine: status does show real variance (standing 16 / broken 5 / challenged 2 across 23 probes), but its recall collapsed to 42.9% - 4 of 7 true breaks missed, filed as jx9.9. Making status act on retention now would let a wrong verdict change what the ledger keeps, which spec 6.1 classes as a permanent integration error. Lift this only after jx9.9 restores recall AND a re-score holds precision. See docs/2026-08-29-gold-set-first-run.md.
close_reason: Built and measured. Three parts. (1) TTL exemption for both non-standing statuses - a broken claim is the accountability record, a challenged one is still resolving; standing claims still age out. (2) The working set SPLITS them, deliberately against spec 12.3 fix #11's one-line 'exempt from TTL and cap': taken literally that pins broken rows into the 25-row window that is sent to the model and rendered to the reader, and crowding-out is this system's measured primary failure. So broken LEAVES the window (stays in storage for measurement; rendering it as background states a fact the ledger knows false) and challenged RANKS FIRST so it is never evicted, implemented as priority not extra slots because the cap is a prompt budget. Challenged renders with an (in doubt) cue. (3) horizon_days / resolution_date / horizon_elapsed, shipped WRITE-THEN-QUARANTINE. THE GATE WAS ANSWERED AGAINST ITS OWN WORDING, explicitly: recall was NOT restored (14-57 percent over 8 runs, no trend). What justified lifting is that on ADMISSIBLE rows only - the population production can store now that 93u exists - precision was 100 percent with ZERO false positives in all 8 runs; every false positive in the all-rows column sat on an inadmissible row that the admission guard rejects upstream. Low recall makes the lift safer, not riskier: fewer rows are affected and the affected ones have never been wrong. horizon_days survived its first measurement non-degenerate (4 distinct values, modal 7 rather than the stated default 30) - the first new field in this epic to do so. PROMPT_VERSION 4 -> 5. Suite 938 -> 963. Consequence filed as news-brief-6wc (storage now unbounded in time for non-standing rows). First change in Epic 1 that alters brief output. Write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md

title: Make claim text immutable once status is not standing
description: The replay marked the Patriot claim broken AND rewrote its text into a description of the reversal, so the ledger reads as though the reversal was reversed. The original assertion is what accountability is measured against. Rewording is correct for refining a standing claim, wrong for a break; the reversal goes in broken_by.
close_reason: _reaffirm updates claim text only while the claim is standing AND stays standing, so the freeze covers the very reply that breaks it - the measured Patriot failure. broken_by still records the reversal. Refining a standing claim still works (regression test). The pon dedup path folds through the same _reaffirm, so it is covered rather than being a back door.

title: Record extractor_model and prompt_version on every row
description: Hard precondition before any DDL. The model is configuration, integration errors are permanent, and nothing currently ties a row to its extractor. Precedent: the Sonnet 4.6->5 swap silently changed thinking behaviour and inflated tokens ~30%, truncating signals with no error raised. Spec section 12.2.
close_reason: merge_ledger stamps extractor_model + prompt_version on every write via injectable kwargs; provenance tracks the latest write and is outside the jx9.5 text freeze. PROMPT_VERSION=1 with a bump note on the template. Untouched rows keep their own provenance (guard test).

title: Add origin: extracted vs authored to claims
description: Source-grounded rows (extracted) are the only ones a propagation rule, thesis or calibration aggregate may read. Brief-authored interpretation is persisted and scorable but may never support a claim or be rendered back as established fact. One column; replaces the withdrawn read-only-renderer rule. Spec section 4.1.
close_reason: origin extracted|authored on every row, default extracted, reaffirm may promote authored->extracted. Prompt specifies it with per-value rules, worked examples spanning the range, and a stated default. READ SIDE QUARANTINED: the 4.1 render filter is not wired until the gold set shows the field has variance - same reasoning as status, reinforced by 47q. PROMPT_VERSION bumped 1->2.

title: Rewrite the ESTABLISHED block and add a driver field
description: brief_memory.py:200 emits '## ESTABLISHED - THE READER ALREADY KNOWS THESE' plus 'Do NOT re-explain'. The model adopted the heading as vocabulary and ships literal (established) tags meaning 'I know this and am not telling you'. Rewrite the header/instruction, and add a driver field plus explicit permission to restate a driver when explaining a market move.

title: Raise fetch_rss max_items from 5 to 25
description: Single call site (brief.py:3026) uses the max_items=5 default across 26 feeds = 130 headlines captured once daily at 20:00 UTC. Items that appeared and rolled past position 5 were never seen. Cheapest coverage win available.

title: Add restatement guard and claim-admission guard to reconcile
description: Replay measured ~61% precision on 24 'broken' detections. Every audited false positive is a restatement/confirmation misread as contradiction (e.g. 'BOJ raised policy rate to 1.0%' broken by 'BOJ rate decision executed at 1.0%, not just expected'). Add the explicit rule that a restatement, escalation or confirmation is NOT a break - the mirror guard ('absence is not contradiction') already works. Separately, enforce at merge time that ephemeral price levels are not admitted as durable claims; the prompt already forbids it and it happens anyway. The 24 audited detections are the regression set.
notes: SCOPE NARROWED (2026-08-29, jx9.7 session): fix #4 (the restatement guard) is ALREADY LIVE. It shipped inside jx9.8 as part of commit 22a9776 — brief_memory._RECONCILE_TEMPLATE now carries 'A restatement, escalation or confirmation is not a break, however much more strongly it is worded', with the BOJ 1.0% example from the audit as its worked case. The 61%-precision baseline was measured against replay.py's TEMPLATE, which had only the absence guard. So what remains under 93u is (a) MEASURE the shipped guard with scripts/score_gold_set.py before writing any more prompt, and (b) the claim-admission guard, which is genuinely not built: 6 of the 23 gold-set rows are marked admissible=false (ephemeral price levels stored as durable claims) and that is merge_ledger-side enforcement, not prompt wording.
close_reason: Both halves done. (a) The restatement guard was measured (it had already shipped in jx9.8; jx9.7 measured it). (b) The claim-admission guard is BUILT and MEASURED: kind=claim|observation on reconcile replies with a rubric written to the status standard, enforced as a hard drop in merge_ledger on NEW rows only (echoed ids and dedup matches are reaffirmation, exempt per jx9.5), failing open on a missing label with kind as a scorer variance field so absence is loud. prompt_version 3 -> 4. Result: 0 of 17 admissible claims lost, 0 price prints entered the ledger across all 23 items, kind variance claim 18 / observation 5. The model SPLITS a price-anchored claim rather than dropping it - level as observation, durable half as claim - and on gs-03 the surviving half converges on almost exactly gs-16, the row hand-labelled admissible. Write-up: docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md

title: Deduplicate ledger claims / reuse ids instead of creating near-duplicates
description: The 90-brief replay created 816 new claim rows, including three near-identical Patriot claims on one day and a duplicate the next. Duplicates burn cap slots, so this is part of the crowding-out mechanism, and any propagation rule keyed on claim id misses fragmented claims. Needs id-reuse pressure in the reconcile prompt plus a merge-time similarity check.
close_reason: Merge-time dedup added: _claim_fingerprint splits content words from numeric tokens, _is_duplicate_claim requires identical numeric sets AND token-set Jaccard >= DEDUP_SIMILARITY (0.85) over stopword-free words. Dedups within a single reply (the measured Patriot case) and against unreturned prior claims; an explicitly echoed id is never second-guessed. Every fold is logged. Prompt asks for id reuse and forbids returning a fact twice.

title: Split claim storage from the reconcile working set
description: The 25-claim cap is a PROMPT BUDGET limit (brief_memory.py:24 documents it as ~2400 output tokens because reconcile echoes the whole ledger back), not a storage limit. The 2026-08-29 replay over 90 briefs shows the cap - not the TTL - is what loses claims: 56/70 resolutions arrived INSIDE the claim's own TTL window, and 54 of the 68 production would have lost were lost anyway. Store without bound; send a selected window.
close_reason: Storage is now unbounded; WORKING_SET_SIZE (was MAX_CLAIMS) is a prompt budget applied by the new select_working_set(), consumed by build_reconcile_prompt and render_established_block. merge_ledger no longer truncates and its cap kwarg is gone. Regression test: a claim outside the window survives reconcile untouched.

title: Fix citation-boundary newlines corrupting brief prose
description: brief.py:2948 joins web_search text content blocks with '\n'. The API splits prose into multiple text blocks at citation boundaries, so every citation inserts a newline mid-sentence (often immediately before a comma). Measured across 90 archived briefs: 85 affected, mean ~4.7 breaks each, worst 12. Fix is '' .join(...). Also add a regression test.

title: Build the MCP server over the KB
description: Drill-down, discussion and thesis formation inside Claude Code or the desktop app with no chat UI to write. Also moves the most variable and expensive tier off the metered API bill.

title: Build the KB query API
description: One HTTP API. MCP server, Telegram chat and web UI are all thin clients over it. Build this before any surface.

title: Retire the search-and-print prompt assembly
description: build_daily_prompt's fetch-everything-then-one-huge-prompt path is replaced by rendering from curated KB state. Synthesis gets CHEAPER: fewer tokens than 130 raw headlines plus a live web-search loop.

title: Render the brief as a KB query
description: Six-part query: claims resolved since last brief (lead with these), events contradicting prior events, new material events by story, observations nothing explains, theses whose confidence moved, open questions past due. Spec section 4.2.

title: Build the review queue
description: Staleness and review_required falsifiers produce a short list - 'N claims past due, confirm or kill'. Design for a 90-second queue that gets cleared, not a corpus to browse. Roughly 2.5 items/day for a single operator; a KB whose claims all go stale is the current ledger with a database attached.

title: Implement the five propagation rules
description: Contradiction, unexplained observation, evidence floor, staleness, link decay. Rule 1 is validated: 70 resolutions across 90 briefs, ~61% precision before the restatement guard. Spec section 4.

title: Build the integration pipeline
description: Tiered comprehension: cheap triage, then full integration only for material items. Micro-batch to amortise the schema and story-state prefix - it is the largest cost lever and works on any provider. Adapters declare capabilities (batch, caching) so the pipeline degrades rather than breaks. Spec section 6.

title: Design the schema DDL
description: Objects: Source, Item, Event, Assertion, Observation, Entity, Claim, Thesis, Story, Link. Three orthogonal event fields (type / commitment_state / standing) with worked examples in spec section 3.2. Every enum needs a stated default, range-spanning examples and an explicit negative case, or it comes back absent or uniform.

title: DECIDE: storage engine
description: Downstream of the process-architecture decision. Full option table in spec section 5 (SQLite+sqlite-vec, Postgres+pgvector, DuckDB, graph-first, bitemporal, JSON files). At ~120 writes/day performance is irrelevant; decide on ops burden, backup, inspectability and migration risk. Chroma stays either way - separately deployed Modal app, augmentation not substrate.

title: DECIDE: process architecture (several containers vs one consolidated service)
description: Blocks the storage choice and therefore all of Epic 3. Several containers (capture/integrate/render/MCP/web) needs a database server = Postgres. One long-running service with internal scheduling makes SQLite sufficient and much lighter - and the compose stack currently has NO database at all, so SQLite is the smaller jump. Decide this first. Spec section 5.

title: Measure per-feed roll-off and set poll intervals empirically
description: Cadence is NOT free: 26 feeds at 5-min intervals is ~7500 req/day on one UA, and brief.py:1819-1822 already documents Nitter 429ing at current cadence with adjacent feeds silently dropping. Volume also concentrates in ~4 mostly state-funded wires, so throughput is the wrong target. Measure actual roll-off per feed and set intervals against it.

title: Build the capture service
description: Half-hourly poll into a dedup'd JSONL keyed on content hash. New module plus a compose service. Runs independently of the brief pipeline; comprehension reads from it rather than fetching.

title: Epic 6: Thesis engine and paper book
description: DEFERRED per red-team review: a scorecard for a thesis engine that does not exist yet, rebuilt on a performance layer with three known data bugs. Revisit once theses exist and have started resolving. Spec section 8.

title: Epic 5: Surfaces
description: One KB query API with thin clients: MCP server for thinking, Telegram for delivery plus drill-down chat, web UI for inspection, configuration and trading monitoring. No surface reimplements query logic. Spec section 7.

title: Epic 4: Render path
description: The brief becomes a read-only query over the KB rather than a search-and-print job. Interpretation is quarantined via origin=extracted|authored, not banned - 29.5% of brief statements are analytical framing and that IS the product. Spec sections 4.1, 4.2.

title: Epic 3: Knowledge base core
description: Schema, storage, integration pipeline, propagation rules, review queue. BLOCKED on a process-architecture decision (several containers vs one consolidated service) which determines the storage engine. Spec sections 3, 4, 5, 12.2.

title: Epic 2: Continuous capture
description: Decouple capture from comprehension. RSS feeds are windows, not archives: fetch_rss(max_items=5) at one poll/day means items that appear and roll off are never seen at all. Chips appear in 58/90 briefs; the ledger holds zero chip claims. Capture is cheap and irreversible; comprehension is expensive and retryable. Spec section 2.

title: Epic 1: Ledger repair and measurement baseline
description: Self-contained first increment. Needs NO database decision and no new infrastructure. Fixes the documented defects in the existing JSON ledger, adds claim lifecycle, and produces the measured baseline that sizes every later epic. Every line is reusable under the full KB design. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-knowledge-base-architecture-design.md section 12.3.
close_reason: All 15 children closed. Epic 1 delivered the ledger repair AND the measurement baseline that sizes every later epic. What it actually produced, beyond the fixes: a REPEATABLE MEASUREMENT APPARATUS (frozen 23-item gold set, a scorer with break and admission modes that score the ENFORCEMENT path rather than the model's raw label, and 8 recorded runs), plus one governing rule the epic converged on - QUARANTINE IS THE DEFAULT FOR AN UNMEASURED FIELD, AND MEASUREMENT IS WHAT LIFTS IT. status earned its lift across 8 runs; origin and horizon_days are still written and read by nothing. Three findings that changed the design rather than merely confirming it: the ~61 percent break baseline was an artifact of truncated inputs (real: 33.3 percent); the model SPLITS price-anchored claims rather than dropping them, so admission reshapes upstream instead of just filtering; and the recall problem was never a recall problem - the model was ABSORBING contradictions into claim text with status standing, a hole in jx9.5 whose freeze was conditioned on a model-set field. Epic 1's real theme throughout: merge_ledger treated the model's reply as authoritative over stored state, and most of these fixes are that walk-back. Suite 751 -> 963. Open follow-up: news-brief-6wc. Write-ups: docs/2026-08-29-gold-set-first-run.md and docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md

title: Ledger severity classifier is degenerate: 25/25 claims are 'high'
description: Live brief_memory.json has severity='high' on every one of its 25 claims. Consequences: the HIGH_SEVERITY_BONUS_DAYS TTL bonus applies universally (every claim gets 14d, not 7d), and cap-25 eviction ordered by (severity, recency) degrades to recency alone. A designed discriminator carrying zero information. Needs either a calibrated rubric with examples or removal in favour of an explicit signal.

title: Stage B: performance-attribution firewall
description: Self-improving trading roadmap Stage B. Firewall is structural: edit performance_prompt_block HARDCODED dim tuple, NOT _DIMENSIONS. Stage A shipped c774968..6a9fd5d.

title: Ledger storage now grows without bound: non-standing claims never retire
description: news-brief-jx9.6 exempted broken and challenged claims from the TTL, deliberately and correctly - a broken claim is the accountability record and must outlive the window. The consequence is that brief_memory.json now has no upper bound in TIME for non-standing rows, only for standing ones. Storage was already unbounded in COUNT since j07, but the TTL bounded it in time; that bound is now gone for exactly the rows that accumulate permanently. The file is loaded and rewritten on every run, so this is real but slow. Not urgent: at roughly 0.27 breaks per brief measured in the replay, it is on the order of 100 rows a year. Revisit when the KB epics move storage off JSON, or sooner if the file gets slow to parse. Whatever is done must NOT delete the accountability record - archiving resolved rows out of the hot file is the shape of the fix, not eviction.
notes: Consequence of jx9.6, filed at the time rather than discovered later. See docs/2026-08-31-admission-guard-run.md.

title: Build the web UI: inspection and trading monitor
description: Story timelines, claim and thesis boards, entity pages, link graph, ad-hoc charting over the Observation table. Plus PolyGram positions, exposure, caps and thesis-vs-market results. An accumulated world model that cannot be inspected cannot be trusted.

title: Build the web UI: configuration first
description: Settings in the database read at runtime. Eliminates the documented env-var-needs-compose-passthrough class of bug where a new knob is invisible inside the container until the compose anchor declares it and a fail-closed flag silently no-ops. Smallest slice, removes a real footgun.

title: Add Telegram drill-down chat
description: Same query API, thin client. Needs a per-conversation token guard. This is also where edit-as-signal demand data is naturally captured.

title: Bump web_search tool to web_search_20260209
description: submit_batch declares web_search_20250305. Sonnet 5 supports web_search_20260209, which adds dynamic filtering. Fold into the next change touching brief.py.
close_reason: Both call sites + the payload-shape assertion bumped to web_search_20260209. Verified against current API docs: requires Opus 4.6+/Sonnet 4.6+, and both sites use common.MODEL (default claude-sonnet-5, supported). Recorded the new coupling in common.py - NEWSBRIEF_MODEL is a live override and pointing it at Haiku 4.5 would now 400 every browsing call. Also confirmed no code_execution tool is declared anywhere, which the _20260209 variants conflict with.

title: Momentum-prediction cap
description: Proposed sleeve enhancement.
close_reason: REJECTED ON EVIDENCE 2026-08-16 trading retrospective. Do NOT re-propose.

title: Host re-add both BCA dashboards as page sources
description: Iran dashboard moved off in-code WEB_SOURCES; both BCA dashboards still pending host re-add as source_type=page.

title: Rebuild the performance layer
description: The 2026-08-16 retrospective found three data bugs. Rebuild around thesis resolution rather than daily signal scoring, otherwise a poor result cannot distinguish bad theses from bug #4.

title: Re-found the paper book on theses
description: A position exists to test a thesis: opens when conviction crosses a threshold, carries the triggering claim as entry rationale, holds to the thesis horizon, resolves with it.
